title: Algebraic Effects for Functional Programming
byline: Daan Leijen · Microsoft Research technical report MSR-TR-2016-29 (December 2016 update); extended version of “Type Directed Compilation of Row-Typed Algebraic Effects”, POPL 2017
note: PDF pages match the report’s pages (1–14). The conclusion and references are not broken out. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: An end-to-end account of algebraic effect handlers in a compiled language. Leijen shows in Koka how handlers cover exceptions, state, iterators, backtracking, async and parsers; extends Koka’s row-typed effect inference (with duplicate labels) to user-defined effects and handlers, plus a new way to simplify polymorphic effect types; gives an operational semantics with a soundness proof and an optimisation for tail-resumptive operations; and compiles handlers to JavaScript and the JVM with a type-directed selective CPS translation, so only effectful code pays for continuations. The typed, compiled counterpart to the Plotkin–Pretnar theory, and the closest published design to Kyo’s A < S.
